# Report Templates

Report templates let `yantra ask`, `yantra research`, and `yantra do` publish a model-assisted result in a Markdown structure you control. The model fills typed slots; Yantra retains the authored headings and labels, attaches the run's evidence, validates the values, and writes a `document.*` artifact family instead of the default Brief.

## What It Does

A report template is a local Markdown file with optional YAML frontmatter and at least one `{{ ... }}` slot:

```markdown template
---
name: exec-brief
description: Weekly executive brief
guidance: Use British English. Write for a CFO and do not speculate beyond the sources.
tags: [work, weekly]
---

# {{ title | text }}

## Executive Summary

<!-- guidance:
Lead with the headline revenue number, then explain the driver.
-->

{{ summary | markdown, max_words=200 }}

## Key Risks

{{ risks | list, min=3, max=5 }}

## Vendor Comparison

{{ comparison | table(Vendor, Price, Notes), min=1, max=10 }}

## Sources

{{ sources }}
```

Frontmatter fields are optional:

- `name` is normalized to a lowercase, hyphenated slug of 1–64 characters.
- `description` is human-facing library metadata retained in frontmatter and JSON listings.
- `guidance` is a model-only document instruction. It is not rendered into the report.
- `tags` may be a comma-separated string or a string array. Tags are normalized to lowercase slugs, deduplicated, and sorted.

### Slot grammar

Slots use `{{ key }}` or `{{ key | kind, constraint=value }}`. Keys must match `^[a-z][a-z0-9_]{0,47}$` and must be unique within the file. An unqualified non-source slot defaults to `markdown`.

| Kind                 | Model value          | Rendered result                                                                                                                                       |
| -------------------- | -------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `text`               | String               | Inserted as text at the slot location.                                                                                                                |
| `markdown`           | String               | Inserted as Markdown; this is the default kind.                                                                                                       |
| `list`               | Array of strings     | One `- item` bullet per array entry.                                                                                                                  |
| `table(Column, ...)` | Array of string rows | A GFM table with the declared header; every row must have exactly the declared number of cells. Pipes are escaped and cell line breaks become `<br>`. |
| `sources`            | Engine-owned         | A numbered Markdown source list built from the run's evidence ledger, or `_No sources were consulted._`.                                              |

A compact table template can constrain the number of model-filled rows while keeping the evidence list engine-owned:

```markdown template
# Vendor Review

## Comparison

{{ vendors | table(Vendor, Price, Notes), min=1, max=10 }}

## Sources

{{ sources }}
```

`sources` is reserved. Only `{{ sources }}` or `{{ sources | sources }}` is valid, it may appear once, it is excluded from the model's input schema, and a slot directive cannot attach guidance to it. A table must declare at least one non-empty column.

The `title` key is model-filled when declared. Its trimmed value becomes the report title used in the JSON document and HTML page. Without a `title` slot, Yantra title-cases the resolved template name; an unnamed template falls back to `Templated report`.

### Constraints

Bounds are inclusive, non-negative integers, and a minimum cannot exceed its matching maximum:

- `text` and `markdown`: `min_chars`, `max_chars`, `min_words`, and `max_words`.
- `list`: `min` and `max` count items.
- `table`: `min` and `max` count rows; row width is always checked against the declared columns.

Constraints can be combined across slot kinds in one template:

```markdown template
---
name: incident-update
tags: [operations]
---

# {{ title | text, min_chars=5, max_chars=100 }}

## Situation

{{ situation | markdown, min_words=20, max_words=250 }}

## Actions

{{ actions | list, min=1, max=8 }}

## Owners

{{ owners | table(Owner, Action, Due), min=1, max=12 }}

## Evidence

{{ sources }}
```

Yantra exposes required slot names, value shapes, applicable item bounds, surrounding ATX heading paths, and author guidance to the model through the generated `result_publish` schema. It then checks all constraints again when the model publishes. Unknown or missing model-filled keys are invalid.

### Author guidance

Frontmatter `guidance:` applies to the complete report. A whole-line `<!-- guidance: ... -->` directive applies to the next model-filled slot, even across blank lines or headings. On a line containing multiple slots, it binds only to the first slot. Directives may span lines but must occupy complete lines, with only horizontal whitespace outside the comment delimiters.

Guidance whitespace is collapsed before it reaches the model. Slot guidance is limited to 500 Unicode code points and document guidance to 1,000. Guidance cannot be empty, contain `{{` or `}}`, or contain raw ANSI escape bytes. The parser strips directive lines from the renderable body, so guidance never appears in `document.md` or `document.html`; changing it still changes the template's provenance hash.

The parser applies the same rules throughout the Markdown body, including fenced code blocks. A template-looking placeholder or guidance directive inside a fence is therefore active syntax. Ordinary HTML comments remain part of the renderable body.

### Controlled publication and rendering

The model supplies slot values rather than a rewritten document. Yantra renders those values into the parsed template and fills `sources` from pages consulted through the run's evidence ledger. This makes the surrounding structure and evidence section engine-controlled.

Before publication succeeds, Yantra checks:

- required keys, closed value shapes, character/word/item/row bounds, and table row width;
- every inline citation marker such as `[2]` against the numbered evidence ledger;
- every HTTP(S) URL in a slot against an exact original or final URL in that ledger;
- raw ANSI escape bytes and echoed `{{ ... }}` placeholder syntax; and
- the final persisted `TemplatedReport` protocol shape.

Provider-schema shape failures return `INVALID_INPUT` before publication code runs. Content failures return retryable `REPORT_INVALID` issues with slot paths so the model can correct the same publication. Only one successful `result_publish` call is allowed. If the model stops without publishing, Yantra sends one completion nudge; unlike the default Brief path, it cannot reconstruct typed slots honestly from free-form prose, so a second miss fails with `AGENT_COMPLETION_MISSING` and may preserve the unvalidated response as diagnostic `result.md`.

HTML uses the same inert, self-contained shell as Brief output. Raw HTML is escaped before Markdown parsing, links are limited to HTTP(S), Markdown images do not load remote resources, and the document includes no scripts, remote fonts, or remote assets. If the rendered template has no `<h1>`, Yantra adds the report title as one.

## How to Use It

### Manage the local library

Create a starter covering all five slot kinds, then lint it:

```console
yantra template new weekly --tags work,weekly
yantra template lint weekly
```

Import and validate an existing Markdown file:

```console
yantra template save ./exec.md --name exec-brief --tags work,weekly
```

The complete library surface is:

| Command                                                                          | Current behavior                                                                                                                                                                    |
| -------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `template new <name> [--tags a,b] [--force]`                                     | Saves a guided starter template. Refuses a collision unless `--force` is present.                                                                                                   |
| `template save <path> [--name name] [--tags a,b] [--description text] [--force]` | Parses before writing, resolves the name from the option, frontmatter, or filename, and preserves document and slot guidance. Explicit tags/description replace frontmatter values. |
| `template list [--tag tag]`                                                      | Lists valid saved templates newest first with slot count, tags, and modification time.                                                                                              |
| `template show <name>`                                                           | Prints the raw saved Markdown followed by its parsed slot table.                                                                                                                    |
| `template lint <name-or-path>`                                                   | Parses a saved name or local Markdown path and prints its slot manifest; failures include complete-file line numbers.                                                               |
| `template remove <name>`                                                         | Deletes one saved template.                                                                                                                                                         |

Every library subcommand accepts `--json` and emits a stable schema-versioned JSON envelope. Human `lint` and `show` output truncates per-slot guidance to 32 code points and the document guidance line to about 72; their JSON output carries the complete text. An unguided template retains the four-column slot table without a guidance column.

### Select a template for a run

Use a saved name, tag, or local Markdown file:

```console
yantra ask "summarize this week's delivery status" --template exec-brief
yantra research "compare the shortlisted vendors" --template tag:work --format html --open
yantra do "prepare the launch review" --template ./templates/launch.md
```

References resolve in this order:

1. Explicit `path:`, `name:`, or `tag:` prefix.
2. A path-shaped value: starts with `.`, ends in `.md`, or contains a path separator.
3. An exact saved template name.
4. A saved-template tag.

A tag with one match resolves automatically. Multiple matches prompt only on an interactive terminal; non-interactive and JSON runs fail with exit 1 and list the matching names. A missing or unknown reference reports the available saved names, and an invalid file reports its line-addressed parse errors before an agent run begins.

Templates require a model. `--template` with `--no-llm` or `LLM_PROVIDER=none` exits 1 instead of falling back to deterministic synthesis. If credentials are unavailable, `ask` and `research` warn about the unavailable model and then reject template mode with exit 1; `do` reports `AGENT_AUTH_UNAVAILABLE` with exit 3.

For `ask` and `research`, `--format terminal|md|html|json` controls stdout and `--open` opens `document.html`. Terminal and `md` output use the canonical rendered Markdown; `html` emits the inert page; JSON emits a stable `kind: "templated_report"` envelope with report fields at the top level. Explicit `--detail` or `--length` prints a warning because template structure and slot constraints control those concerns.

`do` uses its normal human progress/output stream or NDJSON under `--json`; it has no `--format`, `--detail`, `--length`, or `--open` options.

## Inputs and Outputs

The template file and the command goal/query/topic are the user inputs. A successful publication creates these canonical run artifacts:

```text
document.json
document.md
document.html
report.md
```

`report.md` remains the operational audit/trust report. `document.md` is canonical rendered Markdown with a trailing newline, and `document.html` is its inert self-contained representation. `document.json` contains:

- `report_id`, `task_id`, and protocol `schema_version`;
- `template.name`, `template.source` (`saved` or `path`), the path for a path reference, and the SHA-256 hash of the complete raw template revision;
- the resolved `title`, model-filled `slots`, and canonical `rendered_md`;
- engine-owned numbered `sources`; and
- reused Brief `metadata` and `notices`, with synthesis recorded as `llm`.

The `slots` object excludes the reserved `sources` value. Editing a saved template affects future runs; existing documents retain only the resolved identity and raw-content hash, not a private copy of the source template.

Template parsing and reference errors are exit-1 validation failures. Common parse failures include malformed YAML; missing frontmatter delimiters; invalid or duplicate slot keys; unknown kinds or constraints; malformed/unclosed placeholders; empty templates; conflicting `sources`; tables without columns; invalid bounds; and malformed, dangling, duplicate, unsafe, or oversized guidance directives. Library `save` rejects invalid input before copying it and rejects collisions unless `--force` is supplied.

## Configuration and Permissions

Saved files live under Yantra's data directory in `templates/<name>.md`: `%LOCALAPPDATA%\yantra\templates` on Windows, `$XDG_DATA_HOME/yantra/templates` when set on Linux/macOS, otherwise `~/.local/share/yantra/templates`. Writes use a sibling temporary file and rename it into place.

There are no template-specific credentials, network permissions, or roles. Running a template does require an available model and inherits the selected command's normal provider credentials, web/browser permissions, consent rules, budgets, sanitization, and artifact protections.

## Limitations

- Saved workflow replay does not support report templates. `yantra run <workflow> --template <ref>` exits 1 with a pointed error; scheduled and nested workflow runs likewise cannot select a template.
- `do --save-as` promotes the browser trace and ordinary replay synthesis, not the active report template. Replaying that workflow does not reproduce the template-shaped document.
- Templates cannot bind placeholders directly to workflow parameters, captures, dates, or other run data. All non-source slots are model-filled.
- There is no remote template fetch, sharing service, registry, or library synchronization; path references and the saved library are local files.
- Template mode has no deterministic fallback. Missing credentials, `--no-llm`, invalid slot publication, or failure to publish cannot degrade to a filled template.
- `template list` intentionally omits unreadable, invalidly named, non-Markdown, and unparsable saved files. Run `template lint <name-or-path>` directly when a file unexpectedly disappears from the listing.
- A whole-line comment beginning `<!-- guidance:` is reserved syntax, even if an older template intended it as an ordinary comment. It must bind to a later model-filled slot or be rewritten.
- Fenced code blocks are not a parser escape hatch. Literal examples containing template syntax must avoid `{{ ... }}` and guidance-directive shapes.
- Templates control presentation, not factual correctness. The evidence ledger proves which pages Yantra consulted; users should still verify consequential model-authored claims against the numbered sources.
